adaptations: Each original healthy variant has an optional -bugs counterpart. Native setup applies raw-redis-startup.patch or aspire-redis-startup.patch only after copying for these counterparts. Both inject --maxmemroy 64mb into the Redis command line; shared snapshots and original variants remain healthy. The startup turn of health-checks requires investigating and repairing startup failures when present.
Copied self-contained raw and Aspire fixture trees, not submodules.

raw, raw-documented and raw-scripted reuse one raw source/build/Compose/license snapshot. Native experiment environment.files selects the README overlay and adds the preserved lifecycle scripts only for raw-scripted.

README overlays are raw (lifecycle-only detached-process guidance, no app setup instructions), raw-documented (manual configure/run/stop commands) and raw-scripted (script usage). raw and raw-bugs use the same raw.md overlay; no duplicate raw application folders are needed.

Historical raw runs used scripted guidance before commit 319104f, manual guidance at commit 319104f, and no lifecycle guidance from caac578 through 35dbfde. Current raw and raw-bugs have lifecycle-only detached-process guidance. Original artifacts must be interpreted with their recorded harness commit, effective file staging and provenance, never today's registry.
Raw control removes inactive ServiceDefaults project/references, OTel startup hooks, and checkpoint documentation.
raw-scripted Bash launcher accepts run-scoped ports and Compose project; PowerShell helpers are omitted to avoid unsafe fixed-port alternatives.
Aspire AppHost project paths are relative to the self-contained fixture.
All fixtures pin PostgreSQL 18.3 and Redis 8.6 to match the Aspire 13.6 integration defaults.
All fixtures select a stable .NET 10 SDK via global.json; the file-based AppHost opts out of central package management for its explicit directives.
Aspire container and data-volume names require a unique BENCH_RUN_ID; no persistent resources are reused.
All documented launch paths use npm ci so normal dependency installation preserves the snapshotted lockfile.
Fixture READMEs document their own launch method without describing other variants.
